summary.patient_symptoms_summary: You reported recent fatigue, a little bit of “flap” (unclear in the recording — please confirm with your doctor), and very dry skin. You wondered if this is related to your recent surgery where one side of your thyroid was removed about a month ago. You came in to review your blood test results and ask what to do next.
summary.doctor_diagnosis: The doctor said your thyroid levels are low.
summary.doctor_advice: The doctor explained that thyroid hormones regulate metabolism (how you digest food and use energy). They recommended starting thyroid replacement medication at a very low dose to bring your levels back toward normal and help your symptoms. You should take the tablets on an empty stomach every day, ideally at the same time each day—best first thing in the morning with a glass of water. The doctor warned that taking too much can be dangerous and cause a very fast heartbeat (arrhythmia), feeling very anxious or really stressed. If that happens, you should seek urgent help or go to the hospital.
red_flags: Heart beating really fast while on the tablets—seek urgent help/go to the hospital.
Feeling very anxious while on the tablets—seek urgent help.
The doctor said this could be a sign your thyroid levels are too high or that “some clots have formed in your body.”
